nodes.label: Module 12 — DoseSpot Integration & Prescribing
nodes.rationale: The medication-order and e-prescribing spine; nothing else in the system imports the DoseSpot client, talks to Surescripts, or knows about the §1311 EPCS regime. M11 + M12 together are the system the hospice nurse trusts at 2 AM.

nodes.label: medication_order Spine with med_class Discriminator (D1)
nodes.rationale: Separate-but-sibling to M11's order_record: modelling medication as just another order kind makes the data blob grow by accretion across three different regulatory regimes (CMS CoP, DEA EPCS, Surescripts SCRIPT), makes the audit denylist unmanageable and leaks EPCS into every signature path.

nodes.label: DoseSpot Adapter Boundary (full integration, not iframe)
nodes.rationale: An embedded iframe loses chart context (diagnoses, care plan, comfort-kit state), drifts prescriber identity into a separate login/timeout/audit log, hands every UI complaint to the vendor, and is a privacy-boundary nightmare for surveyors asking exactly what data left the perimeter. WardenX ships a native prescribing UI with the adapter as a thin circuit-broken pass-through that never logs bodies in the clear.

nodes.label: EPCS Architecture Ships, Certification Gated (D18 / ADR-006, ADR-0019 D1)
nodes.rationale: Building the architecture without the certification engagement ships the data model, audit trail and records-of-application surface today; flipping not_certified → audit_in_progress → certified is a per-tenant config change, not a redesign. A lawful Phase-1 non-EPCS path (manually-signed DEA-compliant paper Rx, or the prescriber's own external EPCS) exists so Schedule II–V comfort-kit opioids can be ordered at go-live — EPCS is an additive transmission channel, not a precondition for care.

nodes.label: NewRx Idempotency Key (prescriber ‖ patient ‖ rxBusinessKey, D8)
nodes.rationale: DoseSpot's NewRx is non-idempotent, so a worker retry without a key would create duplicate prescriptions at the pharmacy. The key captures 'same prescriber, same patient, same drug+strength+sig' with the sig canonicalized first so whitespace and case changes do not break dedup; keying on order ID alone would make the correction-of-record flow self-dedup and break.

nodes.label: Refill Inbox — approval mints a NEW medication_order (D9)
nodes.rationale: Refills are new prescriptions requiring signature, so minting a new order row keeps the audit trail clean and reuses the whole sign workflow; a status flip on the source order would make a CMS surveyor read the new dispensation as a continuation.

nodes.label: Webhook Security Envelope (HMAC + timestamp + dedup + encryption at rest, D7)
nodes.rationale: Defense in depth: signature verifies authenticity, timestamp tolerance prevents replay with a stolen request, the (dosespot_event_id, organization_id) unique constraint ensures idempotency, and per-tenant DEK encryption protects pharmacy/prescription PHI in the body even if RLS were bypassed.

nodes.label: MedicationHistory Persisted but Never Auto-Linked to an Order (D10)
nodes.rationale: Surescripts MedHx is an inventory of fills, not authoritative orders; auto-linking would force a clinical decision the system is not authorized to make. The reconciliation worksheet preserves clinician judgement — the same 'AI proposes, clinician approves' shape as DocLens.

nodes.label: AI-Prohibited Zone for Medication Orders (D12)
nodes.rationale: AI Governance §2.1.1 mandates a hard block: medication errors directly harm patients and 'AI suggests, clinician decides' cannot be retrofitted onto medication mutation without a safety review that has not happened. Every approval gate has a bypass path, so the boot-time validateMedicationAIBlock() check against M32's prompt registry makes the violation impossible to ship.

nodes.label: DoseSpot Degraded Mode — Sign Always Permitted, Transmission Queues (D11)
nodes.rationale: Hospice clinicians prescribe at 2 AM and a vendor outage cannot block patient care. The clinical record — signature, audit trail, eMAR consumability — is all on our side; only pharmacy transmission can defer, so drafts persist with dosespot_send_state='queued' and drain on circuit close.

nodes.label: Per-Tenant DoseSpot Clinic Credentials (D5)
nodes.rationale: One shared DoseSpot clinic would conflate tenants and break Surescripts's per-prescriber identity model; credentials load from the secrets manager at boot with no plaintext on disk in production, and boot validation that every enrolled tenant has credentials fails fast.

nodes.label: Outbox-Driven DoseSpot Patient Sync (D4)
nodes.rationale: M5 is the system of record for demographics and emits events without knowing M12 exists; M12 subscribes without M5 knowing. M5 calling DoseSpot directly would violate the M5 boundary (M5 has no DoseSpot import), and a polled diff worker would be heavier with more latency. The upsert is idempotent, keyed on wardenx_patient_id.
